title: Author living product requirements safely
statement: As a product owner or AI collaborator, I can explain why the change matters and create or revise user stories and acceptance criteria while preserving stable identity and explicit decision history.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Callers choose stable story and criterion IDs; criterion URNs remain stable across wording revisions and removed criterion IDs are never reused.
Adding, revising, or removing one criterion creates a complete immutable story revision that names the exact current parent revision.
Story lifecycle is recorded through append-only proposed, accepted, deferred, rejected, and retired events; criteria inherit the current story lifecycle.
Concurrent revision or lifecycle heads remain explicit conflicts until a reconciliation record names every competing head.
Human editor workflows and structured FILE-or-stdin AI workflows share the same validation, idempotency, atomic-write, and machine-readable result path.
Invalid identity, parent, schema, lifecycle, or criterion history leaves the Saga unchanged and returns an actionable error.
The Requirements page opens directly as its own overview and presents a concise Rationale before the story list, without a redundant Overview child.
Requirement revisions and lifecycle events retain their stated reason so Git history and Saga history together show what changed, when, and why.
